issues.claim: "staff profiles show technicians moving from boarding to pharmacy"
issues.problem: Minor overgeneralisation, not a factual error. Only one profile on the Employee of the Month page shows that ladder (Feb 2020 profile: started as a boarding technician, moved up to pharmacy/outpatient technician); another profile shows one person holding animal-care, assistant and lab roles. Plural "technicians" extends a single example.
issues.fix: Change to "a staff profile shows a technician moving from boarding to pharmacy" or "staff profiles show people working across boarding, lab and pharmacy roles".

issues.claim: "page on-call for emergencies" (Opportunity 1, what it would do)
issues.problem: Minor, non-blocking. The practice's public pages confirm 24-hour emergency availability routed to the main number and 8am-7pm technician staffing, but do not state that an on-call roster exists. Paging "on-call" is an assumption about how after-hours cover works, presented as design detail rather than as a fact or labelled inference.
issues.fix: Say "route emergencies to your after-hours contact" instead of "page on-call", so the design does not presuppose an on-call roster.

issues.claim: "at $28.32/hour (veterinary technician median, NJ, May 2023, x1.25 benefits)"
issues.problem: Minor, non-blocking. The base figure is correct ($22.66 median hourly, NJ, May 2023, BLS OEWS) and the multiplication is right, but (a) the 1.25 benefits load is an unsourced assumption shown without a hedge, and (b) the May 2023 benchmark is roughly two years older than the audit date, so real 2026 labour cost is likely higher and the range is conservative. BLS ECEC benefit loadings run higher than 25%, so the estimate is not inflated.
issues.fix: Add a short parenthetical such as "(wage from May 2023 BLS state data, plus an assumed 25% benefits load; current wages are likely higher, so this is conservative)".

issues.problem: No issue - recorded here for completeness.
